ayahOccurrences.text: يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولُنَا يُبَيِّنُ لَكُمْ عَلَىٰ فَتْرَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ أَن تَقُولُوا۟ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنۢ بَشِيرٍ وَلَا نَذِيرٍ ۖ فَقَدْ جَآءَكُم بَشِيرٌ وَنَذِيرٌ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ

ayahOccurrences.text: لَا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ
ayahOccurrences.highlightedHtml: لَا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ

lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: فَتْرَةٍ is in the derivative form: فَتْرةٌ
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
ف/ت/ر   f–t–r to abate, to weaken, to slacken
; weakness; period between 2 events; onset of intoxication, to be tipsy.

Of this root, 3 forms occur 1 time each in the Qur’an:
يَفْتُرون yafturūn; يُفَتَّر yufattar and فَتْرةٌ fatratun.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
فَتْرةٌ fatratun [n.] interval, period; interruption, break *

(5:19) ‏عَلَى‏ ‏فَتْرَةٍ‏ ‏مِنَ‏ ‏الرُّسُلِ‏ after a break [in the sequence] of messengers, after an interruption [in the sending] of prophets.

entries.label: يَفْتَر
entries.definitionHtml:
يَفْتَر yafturūn [imperf. of v. فَتَرَ fatara, intrans.] to tire, to slacken, to let up, to desist

(21:20) يُسَبِّحُونَ‏ ‏اللَّيْلَ‏ ‏وَالنَّهَارَ‏ ‏لاَ‏ ‏يَفْتُرُونَ they glorify [Him] night and day and they do not tire [of it].

entries.label: يُفَتَّر
entries.definitionHtml:
يُفَتَّر yufattar [pass. imperf. of v. II] to be relaxed, to be weakened, to be alleviated

(43:75) لاَ يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهُمْ وَهُمْ فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ it will never be alleviated from them–they [will remain] in utter despair therein.
